units.function: Customer/developer positioning, feature claims, architecture overview, quickstart, portability, telemetry, roadmap and license documentation.
units.dependencyDirection: Documentation describes server, Web, CLI, Adapters, deployment and policy as one product and links mutable master-branch assets/guides.
units.keyDataModels: Autonomous companies, Agent employees, goals, heartbeats, budgets, approvals, multi-company, plugins, portability and telemetry.
units.lifecycle: Discovery, local quickstart, Agent setup, autonomous execution/monitoring, portability and development.
units.testAssessment: No executable validation. Completed audits corroborate capability presence but weaken several absolute claims; remaining Web/server units prevent accepting mobile, isolation and governance claims as proven.
units.designRationale: Explain a broad AI-company control plane through task-manager language and all-in-one local setup.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs claim-to-test traceability and a narrative centered on mixed human/Agent responsibility rather than autonomous-Agent hierarchy alone.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY for competitor positioning/capability taxonomy. Do not copy brand, prose or absolute assurances.
units.responsibilityConflict: Accountable human ownership, responsibility contracts and data authority are not the organizing model; CEO/admin language conflates business and instance authority.
evidence: README declares MIT and default-enabled telemetry
units.securityFindings: Claims of complete isolation, immutable audit, universal sign-off, scoped Secret exposure and safe rollback exceed current evidence. Completed audits found direct-DB mutations, approval gaps, credential output, partial imports, heuristic scrubbing, cross-instance Secret leakage and nontransactional side effects. Generic production/Vercel guidance lacks a full TLS/proxy/operations contract.

units.function: Prints Paperclip ASCII branding and tagline with terminal colors.
units.lifecycle: Compose fixed colored lines and print.
units.testAssessment: No focused test; none is needed for Company OS product behavior.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs independent branding and machine-readable CLI output discipline.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT. Do not copy Paperclip marks, art or tagline; suppress branding in JSON/noninteractive modes.
units.responsibilityConflict: None; this is a brand ownership boundary.
units.securityFindings: No direct vulnerability; unconditional decorative stdout can corrupt automation output.

units.function: Builds a local HTTP health URL, mapping wildcard binds to loopback and bracketing IPv6 literals.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure helper -> configured host and port.
units.lifecycle: Normalize wildcard to loopback, bracket colon host, concatenate URL.
units.testAssessment: Completed service-health suite passed 7/7; malformed hosts, zones, schemes, invalid ports and TLS parity are not isolated.
units.designRationale: Wildcard listen addresses are not connect destinations, so supervision probes loopback.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs instance-bound authenticated readiness endpoints.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT wildcard/IPv6 formatting, but derive a validated supervisor endpoint and bind responses to build/instance identity.
units.responsibilityConflict: A spoofed health response can misstate execution-plane safety.
units.securityFindings: Always emits HTTP, trusts arbitrary host text and does not validate the port or authenticate the responding process; liveness and readiness are conflated.

units.function: Tests whether an IPv4-loopback TCP port can be bound and returns availability or an English error.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI utility -> Node net and local kernel socket state.
units.lifecycle: Create server, listen on 127.0.0.1, classify error, close on success.
units.testAssessment: No focused test. Completed port-check audit also found no behavioral proof; sandbox denial exposed unbounded probing in a caller.
units.designRationale: Cheap preflight before selecting a local port.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs atomic service binding/readiness with IPv4/IPv6/profile parity.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT by binding atomically or reserving an OS socket; use stable errors and bounded timeout/cancellation.
units.responsibilityConflict: Incorrect probing can target the wrong execution node.
units.securityFindings: Check-then-bind races remain; only IPv4 loopback is tested. Invalid ports, listen/close hangs and close errors lack timeouts/handling; raw platform errors are unstable contracts.

units.function: Resolves a relative runtime path by returning the first existing candidate across config, workspace-server, workspace and cwd roots.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI utility -> ambient cwd, config location and filesystem existence.
units.keyDataModels: Raw path, optional config path and ordered candidates.
units.lifecycle: Expand home, accept absolute, derive candidates, choose first existing or first candidate.
units.testAssessment: No focused test; the completed checks/path-resolver alias audit was REJECT with TypeScript as its only verification.
units.designRationale: Preserve compatibility across source checkouts and installed layouts.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs explicit canonical resource ownership for Secrets, plugins, assets and runtime inputs.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT first-existing semantics. Use typed origins, canonical containment/no-follow checks and explicit layout migration.
units.responsibilityConflict: Ambiguous resolution can bind a different resource than the reviewed responsibility/approval contract.
units.securityFindings: HIGH: the same string resolves differently with cwd and file existence, enabling confused-deputy selection. Absolute paths and symlinks are accepted without canonical containment, type, owner, mode or allowed-root policy.
